description: The aster brand of Multi-brand: its theme picks in each mode. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

aster.label: Aster
aster.description: Calm and precise: teal, Inter, small corners.

theme.$description: The Aster theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base. Info uses blue, kept apart from the brand color so it never reads as an action. Categories 1 to 5 are teal, purple, orange, blue, green: distinct hues for tags and chart series, with no meaning. Disabled uses the neutral slate.

open-ds.why: radius.4: We use a 4px corner for Aster's buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a calm, precise tone, by brand convention. A small radius does this by softening the edge just enough while the sides stay straight. So Aster feels exact and steady, the least round of the three brands, because each brand sets its corners (shape.values) on a neutral base (brand.q1).

radius.4: We use the 4px control corner for Aster's badges in order to keep one role family by the badge relation: here badges share the control's corner. The same small radius does this by giving a plan status the box shape of the buttons. So a status reads as a small square tag, because each brand sets its three corners (shape.roles) and Aster's are small (shape.values).

radius.4: We use a 4px corner for Aster's menu options in order to keep nesting by the relation: the 8px surface corner minus the panel's 4px padding. The inner radius does this by following the outer curve at the padding's distance. So an option's curve runs parallel to its menu's curve, because Aster's surfaces take 8px (shape.roles, brand.q1) and the panel's padding is 4px (spacing.values).

radius.4: We use the 4px control corner for Aster's growing boxes in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving a list item or a text area the curve of the controls beside it. So fields and rows read as one family, because Aster's control corner is small, not a pill (shape.values).

radius.8: We use an 8px corner for Aster's cards and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a calm tone by brand convention. A modest radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve twice the 4px control corner. So a plan card reads as one object without feeling soft, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and each brand colors a neutral base (brand.q1).

The step does this by naming white, as nothing sits above it and no light role reads the floor. So light pages stay as they are, because the floor exists for dark wells below the canvas (theming.values) and the gray ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

neutral.0: We use white, as raised, for menus, dialogs, sheets and toasts in light, in order to keep a floating layer as plain as the content it covers. The fill does this by staying white while its shadow lifts it off the page. shadow.card: We use step 1 of the shadow scale for cards in order to show their height just above the page. The cast shade does this by a 2px offset and an 8px blur at 8%. So plan cards group each offer and lift only slightly, because cards rise too (elevation.roles) and shadows are soft (elevation.values).

shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show floating height, one step above the cards. The cast shade does this by a 12px offset and a 32px blur at 16%, four times the card's blur. So a menu floats clear above the cards in every brand, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and shadows are soft (elevation.values).

slate-deep.dark.floor: We use one step below 0 for the floor in dark in order to put wells and the hover band below a canvas that sits on 0. The step does this by keeping the hue and chroma of 0 at 0.04 lower OKLab lightness, as the slate-deep ramp has no lower step. So a table header reads as recessed even on the page itself, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the gray ramp sets the steps (color.definition).
neutral.0, under content: 1.13:1 from surface.default, so cards and panels stand forward.
neutral.50: the base for content; body text reads 17.06:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.

neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for parts that rise inside the page in dark, in order to show height by tone, 1.22:1 on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. Menus, dialogs and other floating layers take the next step up (surface.floating). So customers see what rises inside the page by its tone, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

neutral.150: We use one step lighter than raised for menus, dialogs, sheets and toasts in dark, in order to show that they float above everything else, 1.18:1 on surface.raised. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule, and keeps what sits on it readable: body text reads 11.86:1, muted text 4.85:1, and dividers and the ring stay lighter at 1.2:1. So customers read a menu as well as the page under it, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the page's canvas, for table headers and wells in dark, in order to show depth by tone, 1.16:1 under content and 1.03:1 under the canvas. The darker fill does this by the depth rule turned downward: what sits lower is darker. So a well reads as recessed and never as a raised card, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the canvas, for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on the surfaces it meets: 1.16:1 on surface.default, 1.42:1 on surface.raised and 1.68:1 on surface.floating, and 1.03:1 off the page. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised and floating layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 8.12:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

neutral.200: We use the step above the raised surface for a pressed item in dark in order to show a press as a change of its own. The fill does this by stepping lighter while the hover band steps darker, 2.01:1 from the highlight, so press and hover never match. So a tap reads under the finger, because pressed has its own look for touch (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

shadow.none: We use no shadow for cards in dark in order to keep shadows on floating layers only: menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts and tooltips. The missing shade does this by leaving the card's height to tone: the lighter raised surface and its 1px light ring. So cards still read as lifted on a dark page, without a shade that cannot be seen, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and cards rise by shadow in light (elevation.roles).

shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light overlay shadow's shape in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 12px offset and 32px blur, at 50% black instead of 16%. So a menu still floats above the cards, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and dark ships for every brand (theming.values).

neutral.why: A cool, firm gray stays out of the way of every brand's accent.
